kpd_wrangler, yes, I read the changelog before upgrading. The answer is not in it, and this thread is not solved. Please reopen it.

I found the cause. PR #812 ("refactor spectral frame handling", merged Oct 22) changed the default in LineList.__init__ from wave_frame='air' to wave_frame='vacuum'. So in 2.5.0 the rest wavelengths are vacuum unless you say otherwise. My spectra are calibrated in air from arc lamps. The vacuum/air wavelength ratio at 6563 Å is about 1.00028, which is exactly the offset I reported (about 83 km/s), in the same direction for every object.

The only mention in CHANGES.md is "Refactor LineList and spectral frame handling (#812)". Nobody can guess from the word "refactor" that a default changed and that redshifts will move. There is no deprecation warning either.

"Works for me" is not a test. If your data is already in vacuum wavelengths, or it is radio, then of course you see no difference. That says nothing about optical data calibrated in air, which is a very common case. m_okonkwo also reported an offset on long-slit data in this thread, so I am probably not the only one.

After being told it was "almost certainly" my own calibration or config, I spent two days believing my wavelength solution was broken and re-reduced the arc lamps for 40 spectra. For nothing. The calibration was fine the whole time.

Workaround for anyone who finds this thread: if your wavelengths are in air, set the frame explicitly when you build the line list:

LineList(..., wave_frame='air')

That fixes it for me on 2.5.0.

To the maintainers (lumenfit_maint), I would like to ask for two things:

1. Reopen this thread, so other people with air-calibrated optical data can find it.
2. Add a line to the 2.5.0 section of CHANGES.md saying the default wave_frame changed from 'air' to 'vacuum', or emit a warning when wave_frame is not set. A changed default that silently shifts every redshift by 83 km/s should not be hidden under "refactor".

I can open an issue or a small PR for the CHANGES line if that helps.
